title: Normal-cone order generators at a scheme near point without reducedness
statement:
Let $F$ be any field and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative $F$-algebra essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be prime, let $A=R/I$ be regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], and assume no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$, where a minimal prime means a prime containing no smaller prime. Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$, $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$, and $S=G\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Assume $G$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $y\in Y=\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ lie over the closed point, and identify this fibre with $\operatorname{Proj}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-pc-proj]. Write $R_y=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_y$, and set
$$h_R(n)=\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}),\quad h_y(n)=\operatorname{length}_{R_y}(R_y/\mathfrak n_y^{n+1}),\quad \delta=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(y)$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-length, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field]. Set $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$ and assume $\Lambda^\delta h_y=h_R$. Let $Q=k[X_1,\ldots,X_e]\twoheadrightarrow S$ be a graded surjection inducing a bijection $Q_1\to S_1$; write $J$ for its homogeneous kernel and $\mathfrak q\subset Q$ for the inverse image of the homogeneous prime representing $y$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Then $J$ is generated as an ideal of $Q$ by its homogeneous elements $H$ of positive degree $d$ satisfying
$$H/1\in(\mathfrak qQ_{\mathfrak q})^d,$$
where $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is the ordinary localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. No reducedness is assumed on $R$. If $J=0$, the empty generating family is allowed.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), basic assumptions (2.1)-(2.2), pp.155-156; Theorem III, p.156; order algebra in section 13, p.168; Proposition 21(i)-(ii), p.181; concluding proof of Theorem IV, p.187. Local algebra form with a minimal degree-one presentation, without reducedness. Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. Intrinsic formulation and embedding independence: Dietel (2014), 9.1.8 and 9.2.1-9.2.2, pp.108-109, https://d-nb.info/1068056037/34. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Write $R=W^{-1}R_0$ with $R_0$ a finite-type $F$-algebra, and let $\mathfrak p_0$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak m$. Every element outside $\mathfrak p_0$ maps to a unit in the local ring $R$, while every element of $W$ does too; the two fraction maps therefore identify $R$ with $(R_0)_{\mathfrak p_0}$. Choose a polynomial surjection $F[U_1,\ldots,U_N]\twoheadrightarrow R_0$ and localize at the inverse image of $\mathfrak p_0$. This gives a local surjection $T\twoheadrightarrow R$ with the same residue field $k$, and $T$ is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring]. Write $\mathfrak a$ for its kernel, $\mathfrak M$ for its maximal ideal, and $P$ for the inverse image of $I$. Thus $\mathfrak a\subseteq P\subseteq\mathfrak M$, $T/\mathfrak a=R$, $P/\mathfrak a=I$, and $T/\mathfrak M=k$ under the quotient map. In particular $T/P=R/I=A$ is regular local. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] there is a regular parameter list $(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$ with $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$. The list of $x_i$ is nonempty: if $P=0$ then $I=0$, so every positive-degree Rees piece vanishes. Its irrelevant ideal is zero and every prime contains it, making the Proj empty, contrary to the given point $y$ [def-nagata-rees-algebra, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-pc-proj].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normal-flat-double-initial-ideal] to this quotient and these parameters. Put $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$ and let $\beta:B\twoheadrightarrow S$ be its specified normal-fibre map; put $C=\ker\beta$. Write $E(T,\mathfrak a)$ for the kernel of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R$. The lemma supplies the parameter identification $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X,Y]$ and gives $E(T,\mathfrak a)=Ck[X,Y]$. Its flatness assumption is precisely the assumed $A$-flatness of $G$, and $T/P=R/I=A$. Keep the variables $Y$ recording tangent directions of the center separate from the normal variables $X$.

source.place: Ancillary source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), section 2, p.153, and the paragraph after Example (4.2), p.157; https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. No reducedness is needed in the source's basic assumptions (2.1)-(2.2). No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: The images $\bar x_i$ generate $I$, so [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] puts $y$ in some $\operatorname{Spec}R[I/\bar x_i]$. Permute the $x_i$ to take $i=0$ and put $D_T=T[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(x_0t_i-x_i)$. Apply [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-algebra-regular] with the nonempty parameter prefix generating $P$. It makes every prime localization of $D_T$ regular local and gives $D_T/(x_0)\cong A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$. Since $\mathfrak M=(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, further quotienting by the $y_j$ identifies $D_T/\mathfrak M D_T=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ with these specified variables. By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], the map $D_T\to R[I/\bar x_0]$ sending $t_i$ to $\bar x_i/\bar x_0$ is surjective. If $\mathfrak r$ is the prime of $y$ in that chart and $\mathfrak p'$ its inverse image, localizing gives $T'=(D_T)_{\mathfrak p'}\twoheadrightarrow R_y$: a denominator outside $\mathfrak r$ lifts outside $\mathfrak p'$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Put $\mathfrak a'=\ker(T'\to R_y)$ and $\mathfrak M'=\mathfrak p'T'$. The surjection has $\mathfrak M'/\mathfrak a'=\mathfrak n_y$ and induces $T'/\mathfrak M'\cong R_y/\mathfrak n_y=\kappa(y)$. As $y$ lies over $\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak p'$ contains $\mathfrak M D_T$. Its image in the displayed $k[t]$ is exactly the exceptional-chart prime $\mathfrak p$ used below. Thus the ambient chart, regular local ring, quotient kernel and residue field required by both numerical inputs have been verified, without assuming $R\to R[1/\bar x_0]$ injective.

source.place: Ancillary source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. No reducedness is needed in the source's basic assumptions (2.1)-(2.2). No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Use [lem-per-permissible-blowup-standard-degrees]. The local rings in its length functions are exactly $R$ and $R_y$, and its residue extension has transcendence degree the specified $\delta$. Its regular center is $T/P=A$, its normal flatness is the assumed flatness of $G$, its non-component condition is a hypothesis of the item, and it does not assume reducedness, and Step 3 verified the ambient regular chart. The hypothesis $\Lambda^\delta h_y=h_R$ therefore implies $\nu^*(T',\mathfrak a')=\nu^*(T,\mathfrak a)$. Here $h$ is already the cumulative length function; the exponent is $\delta$, with no extra summation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-permissible-adapted-standard-basis] to the unchanged degree sequence, using the same quotient, parameters and chart. It gives a finite standard basis $f_i$ of the ambient ideal, with initial forms $\phi_i\in B_{d_i}$, $d_i>0$, that minimally generate $E(T,\mathfrak a)$ and whose dehomogenizations belong to $\mathfrak p^{d_i}k[t]_{\mathfrak p}$. All its hypotheses were checked in Steps 1–4. The choice of this basis is the substantive adapted-basis assertion; arbitrary initial generators need not have this property.

proof.text: Step 2 identifies $E(T,\mathfrak a)$ with $Ck[X,Y]$, and Step 5 says it is generated by the $\phi_i\in B$. Hence the $\phi_i$ generate $C$: for any $c\in C$, express $c=\sum a_i(X,Y)\phi_i(X)$ in $k[X,Y]$ and substitute $Y=0$. Each $\phi_i\in C$, since it belongs to $Ck[X,Y]$ and evaluation at $Y=0$ sends that ideal into $C$. This is a polynomial retraction, so it proves generation in $B$ itself.

source.place: Ancillary source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), agent evaluation-at-zero deduction from the normal-flat comparison and Proposition 21; https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. No reducedness is needed in the source's basic assumptions (2.1)-(2.2). No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q_B$ be the inverse image in $B$ of the homogeneous prime of $y$. Since $X_0\notin\mathfrak q_B$, write $B[X_0^{-1}]=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r][X_0,X_0^{-1}]$ by $X_i=X_0t_i$. Homogeneity gives $\mathfrak q_B B[X_0^{-1}]=\mathfrak p\,k[t][X_0,X_0^{-1}]$: each homogeneous $g$ is $X_0^{\deg g}g(1,t)$, and the degree-zero chart prime is $\mathfrak p$. In particular $\mathfrak q_BB[X_0^{-1}]\cap k[t]=\mathfrak p$. For every $b(t)\notin\mathfrak p$, its substitution $b(X_1/X_0,\ldots,X_r/X_0)$ is outside the extended prime, so is a unit in $B_{\mathfrak q_B}$. This defines the fraction map $k[t]_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q_B}$; it is local because the elements of $\mathfrak p$ map into $\mathfrak q_BB_{\mathfrak q_B}$. Step 5 and $\phi_i=X_0^{d_i}\phi_i(1,t)$ give $\phi_i/1\in(\mathfrak q_BB_{\mathfrak q_B})^{d_i}$ by multiplying the fractions in the indicated ideal power. This proves the required ordinary-localization order condition for the ambient generators.

source.place: Ancillary source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), agent chart fraction calculation; compares the dehomogeneous order convention in section 13 with ordinary homogeneous-prime localization; https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. No reducedness is needed in the source's basic assumptions (2.1)-(2.2). No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Compare $B\twoheadrightarrow S$ with the specified $\alpha:Q\twoheadrightarrow S$. The degree-one map of $\alpha$ is bijective. Lift the images of the variables of $Q$ to elements $L_1,\ldots,L_e\in B_1$, and choose a basis $V_1,\ldots,V_a$ of $\ker(B_1\to S_1)$. These form a basis of $B_1$: subtracting the unique linear combination of the $L_j$ with the same image puts any vector in the kernel, and a linear relation first has every $L_j$ coefficient zero after mapping to $S_1$, then every $V_i$ coefficient zero. Linear change of variables identifies $B$ with $Q[V]$, compatibly with both maps to $S$: their equality is checked on every variable, hence follows from the polynomial universal property. Explicitly, expand each original variable $X_j$ in this basis of $B_1$ and send it to the same linear combination of the variables of $Q[V]$; the two substitutions are inverse on variables, hence inverse ring maps. Let $\pi:B\twoheadrightarrow Q$ set $V=0$. A polynomial minus its value at $V=0$ is in $(V)$, so $C=(V)+JB$ and $\mathfrak q_B=(V)+\mathfrak qB=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Applying $\pi$ to Step 6 proves that $H_i=\pi(\phi_i)$ generate $J$. Since the substitution is linear and homogeneous, each nonzero $H_i$ is homogeneous of degree $d_i>0$.

source.place: Ancillary source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), agent linear-algebra comparison of minimal and nonminimal normal-fibre presentations; compare Dietel (2014), Lemma 9.1.8, p.108; https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. No reducedness is needed in the source's basic assumptions (2.1)-(2.2). No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: The equality $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q_B$ gives a local map $B_{\mathfrak q_B}\to Q_{\mathfrak q}$, since it sends every allowed denominator to an element outside $\mathfrak q$. It sends $\mathfrak q_B B_{\mathfrak q_B}$ into $\mathfrak q Q_{\mathfrak q}$. Explicitly, write the membership from Step 7 as $\phi_i/1=\sum_\ell a_\ell b_{\ell,1}\cdots b_{\ell,d_i}$ with $b_{\ell,j}\in\mathfrak q_B B_{\mathfrak q_B}$. Applying the fraction map gives the same finite sum with every $b_{\ell,j}$ replaced by its image in $\mathfrak qQ_{\mathfrak q}$; thus its image belongs to $(\mathfrak qQ_{\mathfrak q})^{d_i}$. Step 7 therefore gives $H_i/1\in(\mathfrak qQ_{\mathfrak q})^{d_i}$. Discard zero $H_i$. The remaining $H_i$ generate $J$ by Step 8 and satisfy precisely the condition in the item. The ideal generated by all qualifying homogeneous elements of $J$ contains these generators and is contained in $J$, so equals $J$. If the basis or $J$ is empty/zero, the same argument gives the zero generated ideal.
